findings.title: Cache status never resolves for delegated (in-memory) credentials
findings.body: The cache status is looked up with `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId))`, but for delegated Google Calendar connections the connectedCalendar.credentialId is a synthetic negative in-memory id (see `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` in the cache repository, and the userId+key based lookup in `getCachedAvailability`). CalendarCache rows for delegated users are stored/retrieved keyed by userId, not by that credentialId, so the groupBy on these ids returns nothing and `cacheUpdatedAt` will always be null. Since calendar cache is primarily a team/organization (delegation) feature, the new cache status and delete-cache UI will silently never appear for the main audience of this feature. The status query needs a userId-based path (mirroring `getCachedAvailability`) to cover delegated credentials.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status
findings.body: After a successful `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache` call, only `onSuccess?.()` (the parent's `onChanged`) is invoked. Unlike the sibling `disconnectMutation`, which explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, the deleteCache mutation never invalidates that query. `onChanged` in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is the caller's callback and does not refetch the tRPC `connectedCalendars` query, so after deleting the cache the 'Cache Status' row and 'Last updated' timestamp remain visible until a manual page refresh, contradicting the success toast.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` instead of the user's locale. The component already calls `useLocale()`; every other localized string in the dropdown respects the user's language, but the date will always render in US English format (e.g. '12/25/2025, 3:00 PM') for all users, which is wrong for non-US locales and inconsistent with the rest of the UI.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no `expiresAt` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows where `expiresAt >= now`, so a cache that expired over a month ago (and is no longer used for availability lookups) will still report a `updatedAt` value. The UI will then show a 'Cache Status' with a stale 'Last updated' time and a 'Delete cached data' action for data that is effectively already gone, telling the user they have an active cache when they don't. The where clause should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match what the cache actually serves.

findings.title: deleteCache throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential lookup fails, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In a tRPC procedure this surfaces to the client as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with the message potentially logged as an unexpected server error, rather than a typed TRPCError (e.g. UNAUTHORIZED/NOT_FOUND) like the other handlers in this router use. The client cannot distinguish authorization failure from a real server fault, and the message conflates two different conditions ('not found' vs 'access denied'). Use `TRPCError` with an appropriate code.

findings.title: No tests for the new cache-status and delete-cache code paths
findings.body: This PR adds a new tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`), a new repository method (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), a new repository method (`updateManyByCredentialId`), a Prisma schema change, and a new UI component, but includes no tests at all: no test for the authorization check in `deleteCacheHandler` (e.g. that a user cannot delete another user's cache by passing an arbitrary credentialId), no test that `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns the max updatedAt per credential, and no test for `updateManyByCredentialId`. The PR description itself notes end-to-end verification could not be performed locally, making the missing automated coverage more significant.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax is macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The `sed -i ''` form (empty suffix as separate argument) only works on BSD/macOS sed; on GNU/Linux sed (used by most CI and dev containers) it fails with 'can't read : No such file or directory' because the empty string is treated as a filename. The update of GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL will error out on Linux. Also note this development-only tunnel script appears unrelated to the feature in this PR and adds maintenance surface to the repo.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on unpinned 'npx tsx' that is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not present in devDependencies (only `ts-node` is). With npx, tsx will be fetched/ad-hoc resolved at run time (requiring network access and giving an unpinned version), or fail in offline/restricted environments. If tsx is the intended runner it should be added to devDependencies with a pinned version; also this change is unrelated to the calendar cache feature and shouldn't ride along in this PR.
